steps.title: Start with an empty canvas
steps.body: New-BGInfoBackground sets the size and paints one colour. Without it, PowerBGInfo draws on -FilePath or on the wallpaper that is already set, and never on its own earlier output.

steps.title: Gradient
steps.body: Two colours blend across the canvas.

steps.title: Glows
steps.body: Soft radial light at relative positions, so it lands in the same place at every resolution.

steps.title: Pattern
steps.body: A grid on top. Dots work the same way.

steps.title: Name the machine
steps.body: Labels and name and value pairs form the text block in the top-left corner. -BuiltinValue HostName, OSName or IPv4Address read the machine the script runs on; this page uses fixed values so anyone can reproduce the render.

steps.title: Pick a theme preset
steps.body: -Theme Aurora gives the text, the panels and the backdrop one look, so the hand-picked colours and the background layers go. Parameters you set still win, and -ThemeMode Light gives the light pair.

steps.title: Add the first chart
steps.body: A chart panel placed by anchor and offsets, the way PowerBGInfo has always placed them. It picks up the theme's panel, type and series colour without a single colour parameter.

steps.title: Let regions do the layout
steps.body: -Region Right stacks panels in a column and -Region Bottom shares a band. Nobody computes widths, the taskbar stays clear, and the layout follows the screen size; the region renders further down show it at ultrawide and portrait sizes.

steps.title: Add thresholds
steps.body: Warning and critical thresholds turn the memory card amber and the D: bar red by themselves, using the theme's status colours.

steps.title: Bring your own data
steps.body: The values move into one function, Invoke-BGInfoDataSource runs it with a time limit and a fallback, and the drawing code only reads $data. The wallpaper looks the same; now it is yours.

steps.title: When the source does not answer
steps.body: The same script with a source that hangs. Invoke-BGInfoDataSource stops waiting after ten seconds, writes a warning and returns the fallback, and the wallpaper still renders.

sources.label: CIM and WMI
sources.body: Operating system, memory, uptime and fixed disks from Get-CimInstance. Read-only, and no module to install.

sources.label: Registry
sources.body: The Windows release and build, and values your build or asset process wrote under its own key.

sources.label: Active Directory
sources.body: The signed-in user's department and title, and the computer's description and owner, from the ActiveDirectory module.

sources.label: REST API
sources.body: A CMDB or ticketing API through Invoke-RestMethod. The function runs in its own runspace, so it gets the computer name through -ArgumentList.

sources.label: Monitoring export
sources.body: JSON and CSV files that a monitoring tool already exports, read with ConvertFrom-Json and Import-Csv.

sources.label: Swap a built-in helper
sources.body: Get-BGInfoSystemInfo returns plain data. A function of your own that returns the same property names replaces it without touching the layout.
